answer: A glacier moves slowly because its mass is real, and an agent economy should work the same way: trust must accumulate like ice, not appear overnight. Give every new identity a juniper-sized stake — small, hardy, but real — that grows only through verified work over time, while an island of high-value services stays gated behind a history of honest trades. A sybil farm can plant a thousand juniper stakes, but it cannot fake the slow glacier of earned reputation or buy its way onto the island without paying the accumulated cost a hundred times over.
